title: The Biggest World Cup Ever Is Coming — and It’s Right in Our Backyard!
summary: Have you ever kicked a soccer ball and dreamed of scoring the winning goal in the World Cup? Well, get ready, because the biggest World Cup ever is about to kick off — and it’s happening right here in North America! For the first time since 1994, the FIFA Men’s World Cup returns to our continent, spread across the United States, Mexico, and Canada. But this one is extra special: it’s the first World Cup with 48 teams instead of 32. That means more countries, more matches, and more chances for amazing moments. The tournament starts on June 11, 2026, at the famous Estadio Azteca in Mexico City, where Mexico will play the opening game. Over 39 days, teams will battle through 104 matches in 16 different cities — 11 in the U.S., three in Mexico, and two in Canada. The final showdown happens on July 19 at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey. Here’s how it works: the 48 teams are split into 12 groups of four. Each team plays the other three in its group once. A win gets you three points, a tie (called a draw) gets one, and a loss gets zero. The top two teams from each group move on — that’s 24 teams. But wait! The eight best third-place teams also sneak into the next round, making it a total of 32 teams. From there, it’s knockout time. Lose once, and you’re out. If a game is tied after 90 minutes, they play 30 more. Still tied? It goes to a penalty shootout — a super-tense contest where players take turns trying to score one-on-one against the goalkeeper. The champion will be crowned on July 19. Can Argentina win back-to-back titles, or will a new hero emerge? Grab your jersey and get ready to cheer!
why_it_matters: This World Cup is the biggest soccer party on the planet, and with games in our own country, you might experience the excitement of different cultures coming together right in your backyard.

background_read: FIFA (the international governing body for soccer) holds the World Cup every four years, and in 2022 Argentina, led by Lionel Messi, won the tournament.
Estadio Azteca in Mexico City (the stadium where the opening game will be) is historic because it hosted World Cup finals in 1970 and 1986.
This World Cup is special because it expands from 32 to 48 teams, allowing more countries from around the world to join.
Article_Structure: WHO: Players from 48 national teams, FIFA organizers, and fans across the world.
WHAT: The 2026 FIFA Men's World Cup, a soccer tournament with 104 matches, will determine the world champion.
WHERE: 16 cities across the United States, Mexico, and Canada; the opening match is at Estadio Azteca in Mexico City, and the final at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey.
WHY: The tournament is the biggest in soccer, and this edition includes more teams than ever to celebrate the sport's global popularity.

perspectives.description: Many fans are thrilled because more teams mean more exciting matches and the chance to see underdog countries succeed.
Some people worry that the expansion to 48 teams might water down the quality of play and make the tournament less competitive.
Hosting the event in three countries is a huge logistical challenge, but it also spreads the economic benefits across North America.
